newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-FUTRE CONSIDERS PLAYING FOR ATLETICO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FUTRE CONSIDERS PLAYING FOR ATLETICO.

text.p: Former Portuguese international winger Paulo Futre, who retired because of a recurring knee problem, said on Friday he was considering a return to the game, playing for Atletico Madrid.

Futre, who became Atletico Madrid's sporting director after retiring as a player last December at the age of 30, told reporters in Oporto that Atletico Radomir Antic had said he could be a useful addition to the team.
"I have had checks on my knee and right now I feel fine, but of course I don't know how things will turn out," he said.
Futre will spend his summer holidays in the southern Algarve region of Portugal, joined by Atletico trainers who will help him regain full fitness.
"I am trying. Let's see how things look six weeks from now," Futre said. "If it doesn't work out, I'll return to my old job at the club."
Futre, now 31, was capped 40 times by Portugal.
He began his career at Sporting Lisbon before moving to Porto where he helped the club win the European Cup in 1987.

He later played for Atletico Madrid, Lisbon side Benfica, Marseille, Reggiana and AC Milan before he moved in July 1996 to London's West Ham, where he stayed for five months before his decision to retire.
